Milestone 3: Character Update

Goal: Update the substance of the website. These tasks require judgment, research, deciding what matters, and rewriting content, but should not require major visual iteration.

Status: In progress (started August 10, 2026). Begin with the Website Purpose and Public Identity decisions before rewriting site copy.

Core-values context: Freedom, mastery, achievement, vitality, and enjoyment. Use these as an internal editorial filter for Milestone 3 rather than publishing a generic values list. The website should express them through concrete choices, projects, accomplishments, health work, gaming, humor, and lifestyle.

Estimated time: 3-6 hours

Update the old identity:

Engineer · Entrepreneur · Investor · Gamer

Possible 2026 direction:

Milestone 4: Unlock the Game UI

Goal: Add the parts that require design judgment, multiple iterations, visual comparison, and more autonomous agent work.

Before implementation, apply the Walking Decisions for:

  • gamification philosophy
  • visual/media direction
  • what should remain minimal

Estimated time: 6-12 hours

This is deliberately after the factual/content work. We should know what data deserves visualization before designing the visualization.

1. Shared Achievement System

Build a reusable visual language for accomplishments.

Potential components:

  • Achievement card
  • badge/icon
  • achievement date
  • category
  • rarity/tier
  • stat
  • progress bar
  • locked/unlocked state where appropriate

Possible tiers:

  • Common
  • Rare
  • Epic
  • Legendary

Do not turn arbitrary résumé bullets into fake achievements. Use the system where progression/accomplishment genuinely exists.

2. Gaming / eSports Achievement UI

Highest-confidence gamification target.

  • Game cards
  • rank badges
  • peak rating/rank
  • notable achievements
  • game-specific stats
  • software/bot accomplishments
  • visual hierarchy for meaningful vs casual games

3. Health / Biohacking Character Sheet

Possible RPG-style structure:

  • current character overview
  • Strength
  • Body Composition
  • Cardio
  • Sleep
  • Mobility
  • Health
  • notable PRs
  • historical achievements
  • current goals/quests

The exact stats should be decided from meaningful data, not because six RPG bars look cool.

4. Travel Exploration UI

Potentially the strongest visual feature.

  • world exploration map
  • visited countries
  • visited cities
  • country/city detail interaction
  • exploration %
  • continent completion
  • current nomad location/base
  • travel achievements

Goal: make travel feel like world-map exploration, not an iframe dump.

5. Current Quests UI

Turn the “Now” section into lightweight current quests.

Examples:

  • Colonist
  • Personal OS
  • Health goal
  • AI learning

Possible fields:

  • status
  • progress
  • start date
  • objective
  • latest update

6. Projects / Companies

Test a quest/completion presentation for selected projects:

  • project card
  • objective
  • outcome
  • relevant stats
  • active/completed/archive status

Avoid making serious company information look like a parody game interface.

7. Visual / Media Upgrade

  • Add photos only where they improve the page
  • Add selected project screenshots/product visuals
  • Add game artwork/icons where appropriate
  • Add travel imagery where appropriate
  • Avoid visual clutter
  • Preserve a consistent visual language across old and new content

8. Home Page Integration

Home should remain clean.

  • Use only subtle game-language/components
  • Do not turn the entire homepage into a game HUD
  • Surface a few strongest stats/achievements
  • Link into richer gamified pages

9. First-Impression Design Pass

  • Make the most important identity/proof visually dominant
  • Avoid equal visual weight for every accomplishment
  • Ensure gamification strengthens the personal narrative rather than distracting from it
  • Verify the homepage still works for people who do not care about games
  • Keep important claims near useful context/proof
  • Make current work visually distinct from historical achievements
  • Make the site feel intentionally personal rather than template-driven

Design Loop

For each major component:

  1. Define information it needs to communicate.
  2. Ask Codex to inspect existing styles/components.
  3. Produce 1-3 implementation directions.
  4. Build one.
  5. View it on desktop + mobile.
  6. Identify what feels wrong.
  7. Iterate.
  8. Reuse the component elsewhere only after it works.

Milestone Exit Test

The website still feels like a clean personal website, but progression, achievements, stats, and exploration behave like a video game where appropriate.

Maintainability

  • Set up a local subscription-backed Codex model router for routine work: route simple tasks to Terra and planning, research, complex debugging, or high-stakes work to Sol/Sol High. Use the ChatGPT-authenticated Codex CLI (not the API), so usage counts against the normal Codex subscription allowance; keep the routing rules editable and review them after real use.
  • Keep structured data separate from presentation where useful

  • Record anything learned that should carry into the Personal OS project

First-Impression Acceptance Tests

Test the final production site with people who do not already know the full story.

15-second test

  • Can they say who Goku is?
  • Can they say what he does?
  • Can they name a major accomplishment?
  • Can they say what makes him unusual?

60-second test

  • Can they explain the main life/career narrative?
  • Can they explain what he is doing now?
  • Do they understand why Colonist matters?
  • Do gaming/engineering/biohacking/AI feel like one coherent person?
  • Do they know what they would click next?

Trust test

  • Do major claims feel credible?
  • Is evidence/context available where needed?
  • Does anything read as unsupported bragging or exaggeration?
  • Does any page create an unintended reputation signal?

Personality test

  • Is the site memorable?
  • Does it feel like Goku rather than a generic founder template?
  • Is intentional weirdness preserved?
  • Is it understandable to someone outside gaming/tech?

Freshness test

  • Is current vs historical obvious?
  • Are old metrics dated?
  • Is current status/projects easy to update?
  • Is any content likely to become misleading within 6-12 months?

Final Verification

  • Clean build
  • No unexpected console/build errors
  • Production deploy succeeds
  • Check production, not just localhost
  • Git working tree clean
  • All intended changes merged
  • No forgotten temporary branches/files
